PARIS, France (CNN) -- In a city renowned as the birthplace of the avant-garde, keeping pace with the latest trends can prove a formidable challenge. Herewith a brief guide to what is currently captivating the French capital.

**Tecktonik**

Parisian youths are devoted to their trends. The latest dance craze sweeping the city is Tecktonik, a fusion dance style typically accessorized with spiked hair and neon embellishments. Keep an eye out for young people dancing in packs outside the Trocadéro. If you are fortunate, you might even witness a Tecktonik/breakdance showdown.

**Le Scrapbooking**

Scrapbooking is the current fashion among Paris' more sedate residents. Head to Le Temple Du Scrap (13 Rue Ernest Cresson) for lovely paper supplies, trimmings, ribbons and assorted finery.

**Bike Around Town**

While much of Paris is eminently walkable, the city's affordable bike-hire scheme, Vélib', launched in 2007, makes navigating the city even more effortless. Thousands of bicycles are stationed across the city at docking points approximately 300 meters apart. The first 30 minutes of any journey are free of charge; a credit card is required to register with the scheme. Once you have secured your bicycle, you are ready to glide along the cobbled streets of Montmartre and course alongside the Seine.

**Café Hotspots**

The classic Parisian image of smoky cafés has now been relegated to the pavements, owing to a smoking ban in bars and restaurants introduced at the end of 2007. Quel dommage! In winter, the café culture's most coveted spots are those boasting heated terraces. You may still light up while savoring a petit café crème, but only if you are seated outside—bring along a turtleneck and a beret to remain both warm and stylish.

**Massages at the Mosque**

Paris is home to a substantial Muslim population, a fact beautifully reflected in La Grande Mosquée de Paris (rue Geoffroy St. Hilaire). The building is absolutely stunning from the outside, and even more spectacular within. Indulge in a massage at the hammam (Turkish bath) and you could easily imagine yourself in Morocco. Afterward, unwind by sipping a mint tea in the courtyard. Do check in advance which days are reserved for men and which for women.

**Subway Style**

Riding the subway in Paris can be a tedious affair. Striking drivers and grimy platforms often render the Metro a misery. Yet the light at the end of this frequently dark and dingy tunnel is the Palais Royal – Musée du Louvre stop, specifically the Palais Royal entrance. Like so much in Paris, it is a work of art in its own right, created by French artist Jean-Michel Othoniel. His design of brightly colored glass beads is an absolute delight, and the nearby Place Colette offers a wonderful vantage point for people-watching: pull up a seat and enjoy.

# Trends and Cultural Shifts in Contemporary Paris

Paris, a city long celebrated for its rich cultural heritage, continues to evolve with new trends and lifestyle movements that capture the spirit of its diverse population. From energetic dance crazes to quiet creative pursuits, the French capital offers something for everyone.

## A New Dance Craze Hits the Streets

One of the most striking phenomena to emerge on the Parisian scene is Tecktonik, a fusion dance style that has quickly become the latest craze sweeping through the streets of the city. Instantly recognizable by its distinctive aesthetic—featuring spiked hair and neon accessories—Tecktonik combines high-energy movements with a bold, youthful sense of fashion that has captivated the city's younger generations.

## Creative Pursuits for the Relaxed at Heart

While some Parisians channel their energy into dance, others prefer more tranquil pastimes. Scrapbooking has grown into a popular hobby among the city's more relaxed residents. Specialty shops, such as Le Temple Du Scrap, cater to this creative community by offering a wide array of paper supplies and decorative trimmings, allowing enthusiasts to preserve their memories in beautifully personalized ways.

## Getting Around the City

Navigating Paris has never been easier thanks to Velib, the city's affordable bike-hire scheme launched in 2007. With thousands of bikes available at stations positioned roughly 300 metres apart, the programme allows residents and visitors alike to travel around Paris with remarkable convenience. This initiative has not only eased urban mobility but also promoted a more sustainable and active way of exploring the city.

## Café Culture Adapts to New Rules

The end of 2007 brought significant change to one of Paris's most cherished traditions. A newly introduced smoking ban forced the city's famous café culture outdoors, prompting an adaptation in how Parisians enjoy their leisure time. As a result, heated terraces have become the new social hotspots, where smokers can still savour their coffee while remaining comfortable in the open air.

## A Place of Beauty and Relaxation

Finally, La Grande Mosquée de Paris stands as a testament to the city's large Muslim population. This stunning building is not only an architectural marvel but also a welcoming destination for visitors seeking relaxation. Guests can indulge in a soothing massage at its traditional Turkish bath, offering a serene escape from the bustle of city life.

Together, these trends illustrate the dynamic and multifaceted character of contemporary Paris—a city that honours its traditions while embracing new ways of living, moving, and connecting.

# Paris: A City of Contrasts and Contemporary Culture

Paris has long held its reputation as one of the world's most dynamic cities, and today it continues to reinvent itself while honoring its rich cultural heritage. The French capital offers a remarkable diversity of trends and activities that reflect both its forward-thinking spirit and its deep-rooted traditions.

## Youthful Energy on the Streets

Among the most vibrant expressions of contemporary Parisian youth culture is the Tecktonik dance craze, an energetic movement combining electro music with distinctive, rapid arm movements. This homegrown phenomenon has captivated young people across the city, spilling out from nightclubs into public spaces and becoming a genuine cultural export.

For those seeking a more contemplative pastime, scrapbooking has gained considerable popularity as a creative hobby. This craft allows Parisians to preserve memories and express their artistic sensibilities, demonstrating that the city's creative energy extends well beyond its famous galleries and museums.

Practical innovation has also transformed daily life in Paris. The Vélib bike-hire scheme has revolutionized urban mobility, offering residents and visitors a convenient, eco-friendly way to navigate the city's charming streets and boulevards. With stations throughout the capital, this self-service system embodies the modern Parisian commitment to sustainable living.

## The Evolving Café Culture

The quintessential Parisian café remains a cornerstone of daily life, though it has adapted to changing times. The 2007 smoking ban significantly altered the atmosphere of these beloved establishments, moving smokers to outdoor terraces and creating cleaner interior environments. Rather than diminishing café culture, this change has reshaped it, preserving the tradition of lingering over coffee while accommodating contemporary health consciousness.

## Moments of Relaxation

For visitors and locals seeking respite from the urban pace, La Grande Mosquée offers a serene escape. Here, one can enjoy a relaxing traditional massage, experiencing a moment of tranquility that reflects the city's multicultural character and its appreciation for wellness and self-care.

## A City for Everyone

Whether one seeks the pulsing energy of youth movements, the satisfaction of creative hobbies, practical modern conveniences, timeless café traditions, or peaceful relaxation, the French capital delivers experiences to suit every taste. This ability to embrace innovation while cherishing tradition ensures that Paris remains an endlessly fascinating destination, offering something meaningful for every type of visitor.

# Paris Reimagined: The City of Light Dances to a New Beat

*By CNN Travel*

Paris has always been a city that reinvents itself while honoring its timeless soul. This season, the French capital pulses with fresh energy—from spontaneous street dancing to cycling revolutions and café culture that's being redefined by a new generation. Here's your guide to experiencing Paris the way locals are living it right now.

## The Dance Renaissance Sweeping the Streets

Walk along the Seine on any warm evening and you might stumble upon impromptu dance gatherings that have become the city's worst-kept secret. The **guinguette** tradition—open-air riverside dancing that dates back centuries—has roared back to life with a modern twist.

At locations like the quays near Jardin Tino Rossi, crowds gather for tango, salsa, and swing sessions that stretch late into the night. What began as niche gatherings has exploded into a genuine movement, with newcomers welcomed regardless of skill level.

"There's something magical about dancing with the river breeze and the city lights around you," is a sentiment echoed by the diverse crowds that show up—tourists and Parisians dancing side by side under the stars.

## Café Culture Gets a Contemporary Makeover

The Parisian café remains sacred, but a wave of innovative spots is challenging tradition. The city's specialty coffee scene has matured dramatically, with neighborhoods like the 10th and 11th arrondissements leading the charge.

Beyond the espresso, expect to find:

- **Third-wave coffee roasters** where baristas discuss bean origins with the seriousness once reserved for wine
- **All-day brunch spots** blending French pastry mastery with international influences
- **Natural wine bars** doubling as coffee houses, blurring the line between morning and evening rituals

The Canal Saint-Martin area particularly buzzes with creative energy, where converted spaces host everything from laptop-friendly work sessions to evening apéro gatherings.

## Two Wheels Take Over the City

Perhaps no transformation is more visible than Paris's cycling revolution. The city has aggressively expanded its bike infrastructure, adding hundreds of kilometers of protected lanes that have fundamentally changed how residents move.

The **Vélib'** bike-share system makes exploration effortless, but the real joy comes from discovering routes that reveal the city's layers. Cycling along the car-free banks of the Seine—now permanent pedestrian and bike zones—offers a perspective on monuments that no bus tour can match.

Popular cycling itineraries include:

- The **Coulée Verte** elevated greenway (the inspiration for New York's High Line)
- Canal-side paths connecting northeastern neighborhoods
- Weekend loops through the **Bois de Vincennes** and **Bois de Boulogne**

Sunday mornings, when certain streets close to cars entirely, have become a cyclist's paradise.

## Hidden Gems Away from the Crowds

The savviest travelers know that Paris rewards those who wander beyond the obvious landmarks.

**Covered Passages:** The 19th-century *passages couverts*—ornate glass-roofed arcades—remain wonderfully underexplored. Passage des Panoramas and Galerie Vivienne offer atmospheric shopping and dining frozen in a more elegant era.

**Village-Like Neighborhoods:** Districts like **La Butte-aux-Cailles** in the 13th arrondissement feel like a small town within the metropolis, with street art, cobblestone lanes, and charming bistros far from tourist prices.

**Rooftop Views:** Skip the crowds and seek out lesser-known vantage points. The terrace at **Galeries Lafayette** offers free panoramic views, while various rooftop bars provide sunset perspectives without the Eiffel Tower lines.

**Secret Gardens:** The **Promenade Plantée** and hidden courtyards throughout the Marais offer green escapes that most visitors never discover.

## The Takeaway

Paris in this moment is a city balancing reverence for its heritage with genuine appetite for reinvention. Whether you're joining strangers for a riverside dance, pedaling along a canal at golden hour, or sipping expertly crafted coffee in a converted workshop, the message is clear: the City of Light continues to shine—brighter and more dynamic than ever.

*Pack comfortable shoes, an open mind, and prepare to move to the rhythm of a Paris that's simultaneously ancient and utterly of the moment.*

---

**If You Go:**
- **Best time to visit:** Late spring through early fall for outdoor dancing and cycling
- **Getting around:** Vélib' bike share or the extensively walkable city center
- **Local tip:** Many of the best experiences are free—embrace spontaneity over rigid itineraries

# 🗼 Paris Unfiltered: A Young Traveler's Guide to the City's Coolest Corners

*Your dispatch from the streets where berets meet beats*

---

Bonjour, wanderers! Forget everything you think you know about Paris being all stuffy museums and overpriced coffee (okay, the coffee is still pricey). The City of Light has a young, buzzing pulse—and we're here to plug you into it.

## 💃 Move Your Body: Dance Trends

Paris has always been a dance city, but here's what's got young feet moving:

- **Hip-hop & Street Dance** — The Parisian street dance scene is legendary. Head to the areas around **La Défense** or **Place de la République**, where impromptu battles and cyphers pop up.
- **Electro Swing** — A quirky blend of vintage jazz and electronic beats that's perfectly *très* Parisian. Look for pop-up nights around the **Canal Saint-Martin**.
- **Salsa by the Seine** — On warm evenings, the riverbanks near **Quai Saint-Bernard** transform into open-air dance floors. No partner? No problem—locals are friendly.

## 🎨 Hobbies That Are Having a Moment

- **Film Photography** — Analog is *back*, baby. Young Parisians are toting vintage cameras and hunting for the perfect grainy shot.
- **Vinyl Digging** — Record shops in the **11th arrondissement** are treasure troves.
- **Urban Sketching** — Grab a notebook and join the crowds doodling street scenes in **Montmartre**.
- **Thrifting (Friperie Culture)** — Second-hand fashion is huge. The **Marais** district is thrift heaven.

## 🚲 Getting Around Like a Local

- **Vélib' Bikes** — The city's bike-share system is your best friend. Snag one, pedal along the Seine, feel infinitely cooler.
- **Métro Savvy** — Download the **Citymapper** app. Grab a **Navigo Easy** card for smooth swiping. Avoid rush hour (8–9 AM, 6–7 PM) unless you enjoy sardine impressions.
- **Walk It** — Honestly? Paris is a walking city. The best discoveries happen on foot.
- **E-Scooters** — Available but check current regulations, as rules have tightened.

## 📍 Cool Spots to Bookmark

| Vibe | Where to Go |
|------|-------------|
| **Hip & Artsy** | Canal Saint-Martin — picnic on the banks |
| **Bohemian** | Montmartre — minus the tourist trap streets |
| **Trendy Eats** | Rue Sainte-Anne (Little Tokyo) for ramen |
| **Nightlife** | Belleville & Oberkampf for bars |
| **Green Escape** | Parc des Buttes-Chaumont — the local favorite |

## ☕ Pro Tips from the Streets

- **Café culture is a sport.** Order one coffee, sit for two hours, watch the world go by. That's the whole point.
- **"Bonjour" is magic.** Greet shopkeepers before asking anything—it's the golden rule.
- **Sundays are for markets.** Wander a *marché* and eat your weight in cheese.

---

*So pack light, keep your metro card handy, and remember: in Paris, being effortlessly cool is basically the local language. Now go get lost (the good kind).*

**À bientôt!** 🥐✨

---

# The Insider's Paris: A Guide to the City's Coolest Undercurrents

Forget the tour buses and the queue-and-shuffle at the Mona Lisa. The real Paris pulses in its bike lanes, its steamy hammams, and the electric energy of its youth culture. Here's your guide to experiencing the city like someone who actually lives here.

## Tecktonik: Paris Dances to Its Own Beat

Born in the clubs of the Parisian suburbs, **Tecktonik** is the homegrown dance phenomenon that has taken over the city's youth. Think frenetic arm movements, sharp angular gestures, and a hypnotic blend of electro house and hardstyle beats. The look is unmistakable: skinny jeans, neon accents, and gravity-defying hair.

**Insider tip:** Head to the clubs around **Bastille** and **Oberkampf** on weekend nights to catch dancers in their element. Even if you don't join in, the spectacle alone is worth the trip.

## The Quiet Craze: Scrapbooking, French Style

It might surprise you, but the American import of **scrapbooking** has found a devoted following among stylish Parisians. Small ateliers and craft boutiques have popped up, offering beautiful papers, vintage embellishments, and workshops where locals gather to document their lives with characteristic French elegance.

**Where to go:** Seek out the specialty craft shops in the **Marais**, where the emphasis is always on aesthetic refinement over sentimental clutter.

## Vélib': Two Wheels to Freedom

The city's revolutionary bike-sharing scheme has transformed how Parisians move. With thousands of stations dotting the city, you can grab a sturdy grey **Vélib'** bike and glide from the Louvre to the Canal Saint-Martin in minutes.

**How it works:** Purchase a short-term subscription, then grab any available bike. The first half-hour is essentially free, so hop between stations to keep costs down.

**Insider route:** Cycle along the **Canal Saint-Martin** in the late afternoon, then continue up to the **Buttes-Chaumont** park for a picnic with a view.

## Café Culture After the Smoking Ban

The recent smoking ban has changed Parisian café life in fascinating ways. The famous terraces have become smoking havens, while the interiors are now blessedly clear—finally you can savor an espresso without a haze of Gauloises.

**The new ritual:** Sit outside for the people-watching and the (now-permitted) cigarette culture, or retreat inside for a cleaner, more contemplative experience. Try the classic cafés of **Saint-Germain-des-Prés** to feel the shift firsthand.

## Steam and Serenity: The Hammam at the Grande Mosquée

Tucked behind the stunning **Grande Mosquée de Paris**, this authentic **hammam** offers one of the city's most transporting experiences. Surrounded by intricate tilework and rising steam, you can indulge in a traditional exfoliation scrub and massage.

**The full experience:** After your treatment, linger in the adjacent tea room for sweet mint tea and honey-drenched pastries. Note the separate days for men and women—check the schedule before you go.

**Address:** 39 Rue Geoffroy Saint-Hilaire, 5th arrondissement.

## Underground Art: The Palais Royal Metro Station

The entrance to the **Palais Royal–Musée du Louvre** station is a work of art in itself. Jean-Michel Othoniel's **"Kiosque des Noctambules"** ("Nightwalkers' Kiosk") crowns the entrance with a whimsical canopy of colorful glass beads, resembling a jeweled crown against the Parisian sky.

**Don't miss:** Emerge here and you're steps from the elegant arcades and manicured gardens of the **Palais Royal**—one of the city's most serene hidden retreats.

---

*This is the Paris that reveals itself to the curious: a city constantly reinventing its traditions while dancing—sometimes literally—to a brand new rhythm.*

# Paris Right Now: The Trends Locals Can't Stop Talking About

*By our Paris correspondent*

Forget everything you thought you knew about the City of Light. While the Eiffel Tower still sparkles every hour after dark, Parisians are chasing a whole new set of experiences in 2024. We hit the pavement to bring you the fads worth your time—and your euros.

## The Natural Wine Obsession Isn't Slowing Down

If there's one thing Parisians are drinking right now, it's *vin naturel*. The low-intervention wine movement has moved from hipster secret to citywide phenomenon.

Head to **Le Verre Volé** (67 Rue de Lancry, 10th arrondissement) near the Canal Saint-Martin, where the cramped, bottle-lined walls are half the charm. Arrive before 7 p.m. or expect to wait—reservations are gold here. Expect to pay around €6-9 per glass.

For something more intimate, **Septime La Cave** (3 Rue Basfroi, 11th) offers standing-room tastings that spill onto the sidewalk on warm evenings.

## Everyone's Doing "Le Padel"

Tennis is out; padel is *in*. This racquet sport—think tennis meets squash in an enclosed court—has exploded across the city. Parisians are booking courts weeks in advance.

Check out **Casa Padel** in Saint-Denis, just north of the city, one of the largest facilities in the region. Courts run roughly €40-60 per hour, split among four players. Bring flat-soled shoes and prepare to sweat.

## The Cinnamon Roll... With a Twist

Move over, croissant—well, don't actually move over, but make room. The Nordic-style cardamom bun and its cousins have taken over Parisian bakery counters.

**Circus Bakery** (63 Rue Galande, 5th) draws lines down the medieval street for its cinnamon rolls, baked in a wood-fired oven. Get there early; they sell out. A roll runs about €5.

## Sauna Culture Meets the Seine

Wellness is having a moment, and the hottest ticket—literally—is the floating sauna scene. Nordic bathing rituals have arrived, with cold plunges into open water.

Look for pop-up floating saunas along the canals during the cooler months. Sessions typically run €25-35 and require advance booking through their websites, which fill fast.

## Rooftop Everything

Parisians have finally embraced the rooftop bar. **Le Perchoir** (14 Rue Crespin du Gast, 11th) remains the reigning champion, with panoramic views stretching to Sacré-Cœur. Cocktails hover around €14. Go at golden hour and thank us later.

## A Final Tip

Most of these spots don't take walk-ins lightly. Download the **TheFork** app for reservations, carry a bit of cash for smaller venues, and remember: in Paris, showing up fashionably late is a feature, not a bug.

*À bientôt!*
